newsitem.title: USA: Stock market pauses after setting record highs.
newsitem.headline: Stock market pauses after setting record highs.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks took a breather Wednesday, a day after racing to their 21st record of the year.
Just after 1:15 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 26.18 points at 7,357.23, giving up some ground after Tuesday's 38-point jump to a new high of 7,383.41.

For the second session in a row, the blue-chip index failed to break through the psychological barrier of 7,400 with a rally stalling at about 7,391. On Tuesday, the rally ran out of steam near 7,395.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 12-10 on active volume of 285 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was off 1.27 points at 1,407.94 after hitting a record 1,408.21 on Tuesday.
Analysts said profit-taking cut into the previous day's gains.

Bonds, which stocks ignored on Tuesday, got a boost on technical buying, market analysts said. The benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 7/32, lowering its yield to 7.01 percent from 7.03 percent on Tuesday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.

The bond market's gain followed a government report that orders for costly manufactured goods rose in April after falling in March but that softer order backlogs suggested a slowing ahead in industrial activity.
The Commerce Department said durable goods orders rose 1.4 percent to $175.56 billion -- the third increase in the past four months -- following a revised 2.2 percent drop in March.
Analysts said the report fit with other signs that the economy was losing some momentum in the second-quarter after a sizzling 5.6 percent rate of expansion in the first quarter.
Technology stocks remained active, but the sector was mixed.
"Technology stocks are up but they are not quite the market leadership that they have been in recent days," said Dan Ascani, president of Global Market Strategists Inc.
Networking stocks were stronger, with U.S. Robotics Corp. jumping 4-3/4 at 85-1/2 and 3Com Corp. up 2-7/8 at 49-5/8.
International Business Machines Corp. added 1-7/8 to 91-1/4 after its much-anticipated 2-for-1 stock split.
Analysts said market sentiment remained bullish.
"When technology stocks and small stocks do better, you usually see a bit more positive sentiment," said Robert von Pentz, a managing partner at Columbia Partners.
Ascani said his firm's sentiment indicators were showing the most overly bullish sentiment levels in years.
"When sentiment is that bullish, people will use almost any reason to buy stocks until the rally ends," he said.
The American Stock Exchange index added 1.06 points to 599.50.
